label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: Depth ordering is preserved, but the simplified equipment and sparsely furnished surroundings read as a staged workshop vignette rather than a complete occupied shop.

The pale bench has blue vise hardware and leg-hung accessories, but lacks readable folding construction and visible yellow frame blocks. Its repeated dots read as surface studs rather than open perforations.
The elongated rear bench carries numerous differently sized tan rounds with darker bark borders and tonal variation, reading as a stylized log-end mosaic.

The blue drill press and gantry router have readable basic substructures and correct broad ordering. The left rail-mounted object is a rectangular handled box without a recognizable plunge-saw housing.
Stocked lumber shelves and repeated vertical rods are visible, but the red shelf objects read as solid blocks rather than recognizable bins or tubs; clamp mechanisms are also severely simplified.
A dark, box-shaped stove with a top plate and connected rising pipe is visible behind the rear bench.
Pale panel supports, tan slab worktops, edge strips and board shelving sustain a coherent simplified sheet-board construction language.
The visible gray floor is a uniform studio-like surface without concrete mottling, seams or wear. Render grain does not establish material variation.

Native stem, angled arms and shade meshes form the task lamp. A warm 40-energy area light sits immediately beneath its shade; warm overhead area lights are also present. The authored view shows a bright lamp underside and warm top-down illumination.

The elevated front three-quarter view and bottom callout margin are present, but the saw is cut off at the left edge, the hero bench at the right edge, and the stove body is substantially obscured. Major equipment is not all clearly identifiable.

The original final.png exists and fully decodes as a viewable PNG. The blend opened successfully with 443 meshes, assigned materials, four native lights and an active camera consistent with the delivered reconstruction.

dimension_scores.evidence: Main bench hierarchy and distinctive mosaic are recognizable, but equipment detail, hero construction and workshop density are reduced substantially.
Benches and machines mostly appear supported, but the stove lacks a convincing floor support and several fittings read as attached geometric tokens rather than functional assemblies.
Pale wood, blue tools and orange-red accents preserve broad color identities; blocky silhouettes and washed-out tones weaken correspondence.
Uniform surfaces, primitive machine housings, stud-like holes and conspicuous sampling noise make the result feel like a rough model.
Foreground bench, rear machine row and wall storage retain clear front-to-back relationships and generally sensible separation.
Equipment is broadly compatible in size, but the hero is unusually long and shallow, and the room overwhelms the compact furniture grouping.
Warm soft illumination and a lit task lamp work, while uniform wood, metal and floor surfaces lack distinguishing material cues.
Most principal object groups are represented, but folding hardware, readable yellow fittings, convincing bins and detailed saw geometry are absent or inadequately expressed.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
